label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 06:32:23Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, which does not deduplicate by provider event_id. About 4s later the provider sent webhook evt_000281 (payment.succeeded, pay_000259, $157.18) twice, 0.5s apart. Provider resends are normal. webhook-receiver queued both copies to provider-events/1, at offsets 119 and 120, and the naive handler booked each one (transactions 281 and 282). The ledger stays balanced but is exactly $157.18 ahead of the provider, which breaks posted_exactly_once and matches_provider. Still open: I did not see the handler setting before the deploy, so I infer it deduplicated. I also did not check why the provider resent so fast. Events after the cutoff may also be posted twice.

evidence.shows: Reproduces the alert: evt_000281 (pay_000259, 15718 cents) was posted 2 times, as transactions 281 and 282. The ledger is +$157.18 against the provider, both overall and on pay_000259. The ledger is balanced; the payments and refunds invariants pass.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 06:32:23Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, about 17s before the alert. All other services have been unchanged since 06:30:57Z.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000281 twice: at 06:32:27.846Z from provider-events/1＠119 and at 06:32:28.350Z from provider-events/1＠120, with different trace ids.

webhook-receiver queued two separate deliveries of evt_000281, at offsets 119 and 120. The duplicate is a provider redelivery, not a Kafka reprocess, and a correct ledger handler should have deduplicated it.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings before the 06:32:23Z deploy, presumably the deduplicating handler, so redelivered events stop being posted again. Separately, a human should reverse duplicate ledger transaction 282 for evt_000281, run the money check again, and look for other events posted twice since 06:32:23Z.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated. Kafka holds events meanwhile, so ledger lag grows briefly. Payments, webhooks and payment-confirmer are unaffected. If the earlier setting is not the deduplicating handler, double posting continues. The rollback does not remove the existing duplicate.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with its current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter), then run the money check to confirm the ledger's state.
